feature.title: Rhythm stability outstanding outcomes
feature.request: I want to plan out further research/implementation of the last claude session.  The last agent made an outcomes list and I want to plan out the work for the outstanding items/outcomes

problem.statement: The rhythm stability work shipped with AC4, AC5 and AC10 only partly met and with known costs. Three of six reference tracks still lock or hold a tempo at the dotted 4/3 ratio, which also causes per-play dance speed differences; grid rebuilds remain on some tracks; the bass gate opens late on loosely placed bass and has lost its protection against scattered bass; clip position differs between plays; a real song change at a dotted ratio can go unnoticed; and double time ignores the dance speed limit.
users: Visitors watching a visualizer react to constant-tempo music, who expect no apparent speed changes and the same dance every play
Trevor, tuning the tracker with the debug harness and judging results by ear
Future visualizers that build on the shared rhythm surface (BassPulse, bass gate, tracker state)
evidence: docs/agents/rhythm-stability-results.md: per-track table, acceptance status, known costs, refine-next list
lonley locks 187.5 instead of 140 in 2 of 3 plays; syncopationbass locks 196 and sees a rival at 130.7; syncopation-no-kick holds 180 instead of 135 for the whole track
boundary.ts:131-135 skips dotted ratios with no time limit; boundary.test.ts:211-213 asserts that behavior
bassGate.test.ts:154 records scattered bass opening the gate with it.fails
Clip spread p95 fails on 3 of 4 repeat runs (0.199 to 0.533 against a 0.05 target)

goals: Publish the true tempo from the first lock on tracks with a kick, without weakening the steadiness already won
Make dance speed and bar position repeat between plays of one clip
Close the partly-met outcomes AC4, AC5 and AC10 from the previous plan, or record measured evidence for why one cannot be closed
Pay down the known costs: dotted-ratio song change, unpinned state.bpm, scattered bass opening the gate, uncapped double time
Give syncopation-no-kick a ranked list of testable causes that a builder can try, as a stretch goal
Keep every change measurable: repeatable offline and live tooling, committed rather than temporary
non_goals: Faster first response: tempo lock near 5 s and meter lock at 11 to 13 s may stay, or lengthen slightly, because steadiness wins over speed
Rewriting the tempo tracker around a new algorithm or a machine-learned model
General meter accuracy work beyond what clip spread on the reference tracks needs
Building a labeled public dataset; the six reference tracks stay the measure
Reviewing how visualizers other than dancing-character look
Upgrading three.js or changing the audio capture path
success_metrics: Tempo within 1% of reference, or its octave, from first lock on 8 of 8 fresh plays of lonley and syncopationbass, and 100% within 1% on imyourgirl, syncopationbass2 and summer2000 (syncopation-no-kick is stretch)
First tempo publish within 10 s of sound on tie tracks and within 0.5 s of today on tracks without a tie; meter lock later by no more than the deferral
0 grid rebuilds on all 5 kick-bearing tracks, unless the rebuild follows a real song change
Mandatory: the scattered-bass seeds never open the gate. Target: it opens within 4 s of lock on all 5 kick-bearing tracks, recorded as met or open per track
debug:repeat clip spread p95 at or below 0.05 on imyourgirl and summer2000, fresh and re-select, measured from 1 s after the latest first meter lock among the compared plays
False song changes per file stay at 0.00 in eval:rhythm
constraints: Rhythm DSP stays framework-free, pure, allocation-free per frame, with tuning constants in rhythmConfig.ts or bassGateConfig.ts (AGENTS.md rules 2 and 5)
95% coverage; every spec beside its file; it.fails records known weaknesses and must be removed when fixed
Compare any rhythm change on all six tracks live; offline results misled more than once (rhythm-stability-results.md)
Reference audio is not in the repository, so live-audio checks can only run on Trevor's machine and CI can only run spec-level checks
Bundle is 312.26 kB against a 312.5 kB limit; growth needs a stated reason in the same PR
Each change ships as its own Conventional Commit PR; every push to main is a production deploy

decisions.question: What does the plan cover?
decisions.answer: All outstanding items, ordered in phases, each independently shippable and droppable.
decisions.rationale: Nothing is lost and later slices can be dropped.

decisions.question: Which wins when they conflict?
decisions.answer: Steady over quick: no apparent tempo change and a repeatable dance, even with a slower lock or song-change response.
decisions.rationale: Matches the goal of the previous session.

decisions.question: How is syncopation-no-kick treated?
decisions.answer: Stretch goal. The planner researches potential causes that the builder can attempt; it does not block other slices or the acceptance of AC4.
decisions.rationale: The track is loosely structured and has no kick.

decisions.question: Does double time respect the speed limit?
decisions.rationale: There is only so fast a person dances.

decisions.question: What does capping do to the double time option?
decisions.answer: normalizeOctave folds to 80..160, so 2x is always at least 160 and always over the 140 limit; a capped double time can never run while locked.

decisions.question: How does the dance speed cap apply?
decisions.answer: The goal is that the character never dances faster than a person would. No setting, locked or not, exceeds MAX_DANCE_BPM: on the beat falls to half time over the limit, with the existing release hysteresis. The tempo-unknown rate is capped at MAX_DANCE_BPM / NATIVE_BPM, about 0.97 of the clip's native 144 BPM, so the default calm rate slows slightly.
decisions.rationale: User: limit the speed to how fast a human would dance; if double time causes weirdness, keep it within the same limits.

decisions.question: What happens to the top step of the Dance speed slider?
decisions.answer: Remove the 2x step: the slider offers half time and on the beat, and the double-time branch of the sync code goes with it. A new settings-panel visual baseline is needed.
decisions.rationale: With the cap, 2x would be identical to 1x while locked.

decisions.question: How does the clip reach the right beat at meter lock?
decisions.answer: A short crossfade to the correct beat replaces the long capped nudge for errors of 0.5 beat or more. It fires at the first meter lock of a song (per songChangeCount) and again on a meter re-lock if the error is still at least 0.5 beat. Smaller errors keep the nudge.
decisions.rationale: Removes the 11% apparent speed change; fits steady over quick.

decisions.question: How strict are the success targets?
decisions.answer: Pass or fail as stated in success_metrics. Meter work stays out of scope; if summer2000 clip spread cannot pass without it, record the measurement and leave that row open.
decisions.rationale: User confirmed the framing with its numbers and non-goals.

decisions.question: What are the candidate causes for syncopation-no-kick holding 180 instead of 135?
decisions.answer: Untested, ranked. Already ruled out by ablation: faster-pulse takeover, TEMPO_SWITCH_ESTIMATES, history length, double-lag weight, comb partials. Step zero: read rawBpm and tempoConfidence per estimate, because everything below depends on which case applies. (A) Self-locking hold: isSyncopationRatio(135, 180) is true, so a true 135 needs confidence 0.5 and 32 straight estimates (tempo.ts:315-331), and a close rival lowers its own confidence through the margin term. TEMPO_SYNCOPATION_* was not among the ablated constants. (B) No subdivision test: 180 and 135 both sit on the same 16th grid at about 11.1 frames, 180 as 3 of them and 135 as 4. correlation[] already covers lags under minLag, but peakNear clamps to minLag (30 frames), so straight 8ths at 22.2 frames are never consulted. Comparing L/2 against L/3 support could reject a ternary-looking 180. (C) No bar-repeat test: a 3-3-3-3-4 pattern repeats at 16 sixteenths, 177.8 frames, which is 4 x 44.4 but 5.33 x 33.3. Comparing correlation at 4L for the two rivals could break the tie, and it needs no kick. (D) Band mix: ONSET_BAND_WEIGHTS was never ablated; per-band sums let a dotted bass outweigh straight hats. Per-band autocorrelation would test it. (E) Frame-grid bias: 44.44 frames splits its peak across two lags more than 33.33 does (tempo.ts:125 records this effect), eating into the 17% prior advantage 135 has. Interpolated peak height would test it. (F) Early decision: first lock at confidence 0.2 from 3 s of history, too short to see a bar; deferring a first lock while a dotted rival is close fits steady over quick and also serves lonley.
decisions.rationale: From reading tempo.ts, rhythmConfig.ts and rhythmAnalyzer.ts, no run. Published work supports tracking several metrical levels with periods that are multiples of one another (Lartillot and Grandjean, SMC 2019) and tatum-based comb scoring (Audacity MIR docs, ISMIR 2006 and 2013); no source covered the 4/3 error directly.

decisions.question: If no gate rule meets both the 4 s target and scatter rejection, which wins?
decisions.answer: Scatter rejection; lonley's opening time is recorded as open.
decisions.rationale: Follows from steady over quick (D2); stray pulses are more visible than a late gate.

decisions.question: How does the boundary detector tell a real dotted-ratio song change from the tracker correcting itself?
decisions.answer: By whether the old pulse is still there. In a correction both pulses stay in the music, so the autocorrelation at the old lag keeps its support and the detector re-seeds its reference with no boundary. In a song change the old lag's support collapses, and a boundary is raised. If the probe shows this cannot separate them, no boundary wins and AC6 is recorded open.
decisions.rationale: Re-seeding on every adoption, as the critic suggested, would hide the real changes AC6 asks for. A false song change resets the dance locks, so steady over quick (D2) decides the fallback.

decisions.question: What does dropping a slice mean for what depends on it?
decisions.answer: A dropped dependency counts as satisfied and its outcome is recorded as open in the results doc. If the probe in S4 is negative, S11 is dropped or re-scoped with Trevor, and S6, S8 and S7 proceed.
decisions.rationale: Keeps D1: every slice is droppable.

decisions.question: What is lonley's true tempo?
decisions.rationale: Removes the risk of tuning the tie-break to a wrong target.

decisions.question: Is derived data from the reference tracks committed?
decisions.answer: Yes: small telemetry CSVs and onset envelopes, no audio, as fixtures for deterministic regression specs in CI.
decisions.rationale: The audio is not in the repository, so CI otherwise cannot catch a wrong-lock regression.

decisions.question: How long may a first lock be deferred?
decisions.answer: TEMPO_TIE_MAX_DEFER_S starts at 5 s, so first publish is within about 10 s of sound; expiry publishes the current winner. The probe may lower it.
decisions.rationale: Long enough for 4L of most tempos to fit in the history; bounded so steady over quick cannot erode the first response unnoticed.

options.summary: Break the 4/3 tie inside TempoTracker by deferring first lock until a bar-repeat comparison picks one of the two dotted rivals, and make the bass gate count on-place hit rate over a window, so loose real bass opens it and random bass does not.
approach: Tie-break (tempo.ts finishEstimate): at first lock only, if the runner-up is a dotted ratio (isSyncopationRatio) within the rival margin, defer lock up to TEMPO_FIRST_LOCK_MAX_DEFER_S (about 3 s extra, config). Then compare autocorrelation at the shared bar lag (3x the longer beat lag equals 4x the shorter) with interpolated peak height. Higher bar-repeat support wins; a tie falls to the existing prior. No new inputs, no kick-only envelope, no allocation (reuse correlation[]).
If the deferral expires with no clear winner, lock the existing winner (no change from today).

Bass gate (bassGate.ts): replace the evidence-spend rule with a rolling on-place hit rate. Keep a fixed ring of the last N bass onsets as on/off-place bits (window plus or minus BASS_PLACE_WINDOW_BEATS, widened from today for loose bass). Gate opens when the rate is at or above BASS_MIN_ON_PLACE_RATE and stays open until it falls below a lower close threshold. Chance rate of random bass is about 2x the window, set the threshold well above it.

Tune the window and threshold with the seed specs: seeds 1, 7, 99, 2024 must stay closed; remove the it.fails marker. Check lonley and the other kick tracks open within 4 s via the gate replay script.

Octave and grid (AC4, AC5): with a correct first lock, the 187.5 to 140 fold no longer happens. Also reset or re-seed lastNormalizedBpm when a tracker correction occurs (dancingCharacterSync.ts:144) and make beatTracker.setTempo keep the grid on an exact octave move. Add specs in dancingCharacterSync.test.ts and beatTracker.test.ts.

Small items: boundary.ts dotted skip gets a time limit (longer jump time, confidence 0.5) and boundary.test.ts:211 is updated; add a state.bpm pin spec; computeDanceTiming halves the multiple until it fits MAX_DANCE_BPM, with extreme specs; committed ablation, gate replay and eval fixes from AC1.
Clip spread (AC9) and syncopation-no-kick (AC3) follow as separate slices, the latter recording each cause (C is covered by step 1) in the results doc.

rhythmConfig: TEMPO_FIRST_LOCK_MAX_DEFER_S, dotted jump time
pros: No new data path: the tracker still sees only the onset sum
Fixes the root of AC2, AC4 and AC5 at once
Rate test is statistically separable and allocation-free
cons: Bar-repeat comparison may not break 3-3-3-3-4 style ties on every track
First lock slightly later, which the non-goals allow
Kick-bearing tracks do not use the kick signal that is available
risks: Offline results may not match live; six-track live check is needed
Wider place window may let dense random bass reach the threshold
Deferral can interact with boundary detection at song start

options.summary: Defer first publish while a dotted rival is close and settle it with a two-evidence vote (bar-repeat at 4L plus a kick-only autocorrelation), and replace the gate's fixed on-place window with a Rayleigh phase-concentration test so loose real bass opens it and scattered bass cannot.
approach: Tooling first (AC1): commit scripts/rhythm-ablate.ts (constant override via env map, seeded), gate replay, stability metric in eval:rhythm, fix verdict rounding and Infinity CSV, so each later slice is measured.

Tie-break at first lock: in finishEstimate, if a rival at ratio 4/3 or 3/4 scores within TEMPO_TIE_MARGIN, withhold the first lock (hold 'unknown', up to TEMPO_TIE_MAX_DEFER_S = 8 s), then decide by vote: (a) bar-repeat support, correlation at 4L of each rival normalised by its lag count; (b) kick-only autocorrelation at both lags from a preallocated kick history fed by pushFrame. Publish a rival only if both agree or one is decisive; on a split, the lower tempo within 80..160 wins (135/140 over 180/187.5). Deadline expiry publishes the prior winner, never blocks.

Once chosen, relax the dotted hold: a decided winner needs only the normal 0.5 confidence, not 32 estimates, to be replaced, so a wrong early lock self-corrects instead of persisting (syncopation-no-kick).

Gate: add off-place counting plus a Rayleigh test on bass onsets modulo the beat period: R from sin/cos running sums over a decaying window; open when 2*n*R^2 exceeds BASS_RAYLEIGH_CRIT and R exceeds a floor; close on hysteresis. Loose but consistent bass has high R at modest n; uniform scatter fails at any n. Remove the it.fails.
Octave and grid (AC4, AC5): reset lastNormalizedBpm when the tempo corrects by a dotted fold; beatTracker.setTempo keeps the grid on exact octave moves; explain the 9 s rebuild in the results doc.

Boundary (AC6): dotted pairs count after TEMPO_DOTTED_JUMP_S at confidence 0.5; update boundary.test.ts:211. Pin state.bpm with a dedicated spec (AC7); cap computeDanceTiming by halving the multiple to fit MAX_DANCE_BPM (AC10); crossfade whole-beat clip errors (AC9).
Ship as separate PRs: tooling, tie-break, gate, small fixes, clip; record each in the results doc (AC12).

Gate rule is statistical, so it scales with sample count and has a principled scatter rejection
Deferral fits D2 steady over quick; deadline prevents a stuck unknown state
cons: Largest change: touches tempo.ts hot path, the pushFrame signature and adds kick history memory
Delays first lock by up to 8 s on tie tracks

options.summary: Stop trying to make the tempo tracker pick between 4/3 rivals: hold the first publish until a kick-only onset interval test (a separate side-channel in the analyzer) names the pulse, and replace the gate's evidence counting with a phase-concentration test that random bass cannot pass.
approach: Break assumption: the single summed-onset autocorrelation must decide the 4/3 tie. Add a kick-only onset envelope (kick flux already computed at rhythmAnalyzer.ts:139) with its own small interval histogram; the tracker keeps its summed estimate but its first publish is gated on agreement.

Tie rule at first lock: if the summed estimate has a dotted rival (isSyncopationRatio) within the margin, publish nothing (tempo unknown, calm dance rate, per D2) until the kick-interval histogram has a clear mode at one of the two rivals, then lock to that one. Kickless tracks fall back to the current path after a bounded wait, leaving syncopation-no-kick as ranked-cause research (D10 A to F).

Bass gate: replace per-hit evidence with a Rayleigh-style concentration R of bass onset phases against the beat clock over the last N bars. Open when R exceeds a threshold within 4 s of lock; scattered bass gives uniform phase, R near 0, so the it.fails seeds pass and the marker is removed. Loose but real bass still concentrates, so it opens earlier.
Octave and grid: fold using the first publish only, since the first publish is now right; keep a corrected-lock spec (AC4) and a beatTracker octave-keep path (AC5).
Dotted boundary: add a longer hold time (for example 3x the normal jump time) at confidence 0.5 or more instead of a blanket skip; update boundary.test.ts:211-213.
Pin state.bpm with a dedicated spec; cap computeDanceTiming by halving the multiple until it fits MAX_DANCE_BPM.
Commit ablation, gate replay and eval fixes as scripts first (AC1) so the histogram test is measured offline, then confirm live on all six tracks.

options.summary: Measure before building. Commit the tools, probe which evidence really separates the rivals on all six tracks, then ship the smallest rule that passes: a bounded deferred first lock settled by bar repeat (from O1 and O2), adding a kick-only vote (from O2 and O3) only if the probe shows bar repeat is not enough. The gate rule is chosen the same way, by replay over recordings among on-place rate (O1), phase concentration (O2, O3) and bar-to-bar comparison.
approach: Tooling first: ablation, gate replay, stability metric, verdict and CSV fixes, plus raw tempo and rival columns in telemetry
Probe, in a results table: per track, correlation at 4L and 8L of each rival, kick-only autocorrelation at each rival, per-band sums, and raw tempo over time

Bar-repeat tie-break with deferred first lock inside TempoTracker, compared at each rival's own 4L and 8L rather than at the lag they share (3 x 44.4 equals 4 x 33.3 frames, which cannot separate them)
Kick-only evidence is added only if the probe shows bar repeat misses lonley, because it changes a data path and spends bundle budget
Gate candidates compete in replay; the winner replaces the evidence rule, keeping the clock-driven bump
Remaining slices are small and independent: octave fold, grid keep, dotted boundary, state.bpm pin, speed cap, crossfade

decision_rationale: O1 has the right size, but its tie-break compares the lag both rivals share, and its on-place rate is the family the results doc found too near chance. O2 and O3 commit to a new kick path and a gate model before anything is measured, and offline results already misled this work. O4 keeps O1's size where the data allows and escalates to O2's evidence only on a measured need.

design.overview: Ten independently shippable slices. Tools and a probe come first, so each rhythm rule is chosen on evidence from all six tracks. The tie-break comes next because it removes the trigger for the octave fold bug and most rebuilds, and because the dotted boundary timer would otherwise report a corrected wrong lock as a song change. Every rule stays a pure function with constants in the config files.

components.name: TempoTracker first-lock tie-break

Expiry locks the current winner. Reset on keepRecent and reset.

components.responsibility: Winner from replay, bar-to-bar repeat tried first; bump stays driven by the beat clock

contracts.name: Deferred first lock
contracts.definition: TempoTracker.bpm stays 0 while a first-lock tie is open, at most TEMPO_TIE_MAX_DEFER_S (D16); rawBpm and confidence keep updating; state.bpm reads 0 and visualizers show the calm state. BoundaryDetector.pushTempo is not fed during the deferral, so its reference is seeded from the decided tempo.

contracts.name: Rhythm tool CLIs
contracts.definition: npm run ablate:rhythm -- <wav> --set NAME=VALUE (esbuild onLoad plugin in scripts/, no change in app/), npm run replay:gate -- <telemetry.csv> --rule NAME, and npm run probe:rhythm -- <dir>; telemetry CSV gains rawBpm and rivalBpm columns; dev only, nothing ships, and npm run size shows no change.

contracts.name: Dotted soft boundary
contracts.definition: Per D12, pushTempo reports BOUNDARY_SOFT for a dotted-ratio tempo held TEMPO_DOTTED_JUMP_SECONDS at confidence 0.5 or above only when the old pulse's support collapsed; it replaces the assertion at boundary.test.ts:211-213. TempoTracker exposes the support at the held lag as a read-only value.

contracts.name: Bass gate state
contracts.definition: BassGateState fields change with the chosen rule; stepBassGate's signature and return value, and the BassPulse surface in architecture.md section 6, do not.

contracts.name: Dance timing result
contracts.definition: The implied rate never exceeds MAX_DANCE_BPM; STEP_MULTIPLES becomes half and one, and the danceSpeed control's max becomes 1; DanceTimingResult gains a crossfadeToPhase value, negative when there is none, recomputed every call and consumed in the same frame, so nothing is left pending while the page is hidden; no allocation.

design.data: No persistent data. Reference tempos and audio stay in git-ignored .debug-in.
design.ux: The Dance speed slider loses its 2x step (half time and on the beat remain). Ambiguous tracks show the calm sway slightly longer before locking. At meter lock the dancer may blend once to the right beat instead of running 11% off for up to 8 s.
design.accessibility: No new controls. The crossfade is a brief blend and adds no flash; reduced-motion defaults are unaffected.
design.security_privacy: All client side; no new data leaves the browser. Tools read local files only.
design.observability: Telemetry raw tempo and rival columns, debug:summary and debug:repeat; results doc updated per slice.
design.rollout: One PR per slice with a Conventional Commit title; check on the Cloudflare preview. Clock-changing slices post six-track live results in the PR before merge. New rules stay constant-tunable. Roll back by reverting the PR or with wrangler rollback: a failing smoke run after merge, or any six-track regression found after deploy, triggers it. A dropped dependency counts as satisfied (D13).

test_strategy.unit: Specs beside each file: synthetic dotted rivals for the tie-break including deadline and reset; octave grid keep; dotted boundary times, including a correction at 30 s raising nothing; state.bpm pin that fails when reverted; speed cap at extreme tempos for each step and calm; scattered seeds without it.fails; meterLocked toggling and re-lock for the crossfade; deterministic regressions over the derived fixtures (AC13).
test_strategy.integration: rhythmAnalyzer.test.ts feeds synthetic envelopes through tie-break, beat tracker and boundary together, including a corrected first lock raising no song change.
test_strategy.e2e: npm run test:e2e after each rendering slice; existing fixtures catch errors, context leaks and console warnings.
test_strategy.manual: debug:viz on all six tracks for clock-changing slices, 8 fresh plays of lonley and syncopationbass for AC2, 4 plays fresh and re-select for AC9; look at the crossfade and calm wait in npm run dev. Live plays remain a smoke check, since unexplained differences between plays exist; fixtures carry the regression duty, without the AGC and block timing.
test_strategy.non_functional: npm run size against the 312.5 kB limit, reduced first by dropping dead code; 60 fps check on cubes and trio-color-wave; no per-frame allocation in the new code.

risks.description: Bar repeat does not separate the rivals on lonley
risks.mitigation: The probe shows this before any rule ships; escalate to a kick-only vote, which has a bundle cost.

risks.description: Six reference tracks overfit the thresholds
risks.mitigation: Prefer ratio comparisons between rivals over absolute constants; keep eval:rhythm and synthetic specs as guards; a deadline always falls back to today's behavior.

risks.description: 4 s after lock holds about 9 kicks, too few for any beat-level statistic to separate 32-41% on-place from the 20% chance rate
risks.mitigation: S8 starts with a feasibility check in replay and tries bar-to-bar repeat first, which uses different information. Scatter rejection is mandatory; lonley's opening time stays recorded as open if needed (D11, Q2).

risks.description: The dotted timer reports a tracker correction or a long dotted passage as a song change
risks.mitigation: D12 requires the old pulse's support to collapse; S7 ships after the tie-break and S5, with a six-track false-boundary check; eval:rhythm must stay at 0.00; fallback is no boundary.

risks.description: summer2000's reference is 127.5 by comb and 129 by metronome, 1.2% apart, more than the 1% test
risks.mitigation: lonley is confirmed (D14). summer2000 is not a tie track, so it does not drive tuning; Trevor settles it before its AC2 row is judged (Q1).

risks.description: Bundle budget has 0.24 kB of headroom
risks.mitigation: Measure per slice; a raise goes in the same PR with its reason, as AGENTS.md requires.

risks.description: The crossfade reads as a jump on the dancer
risks.mitigation: Blend time is a constant; judged by eye in npm run dev; the capped nudge stays for small errors.

risks.description: Fixtures omit the AGC and block timing, so they may pass where live fails
risks.mitigation: Fixtures guard regressions only; acceptance stays live on all six tracks.

open_questions.question: Is summer2000 127.5 or 129 BPM? The two are 1.2% apart, more than the 1% test. lonley is confirmed at 140.
open_questions.owner: Trevor, before judging summer2000's AC2 row

open_questions.question: If replay shows no gate rule both opens within 4 s on lonley and rejects scatter, is a later opening acceptable? Plan default: yes, scatter rejection wins.

findings.finding: AC8 and the third success metric demand both 'gate opens within 4 s of lock on all 5 kick tracks' and 'scattered seeds stay closed', while D11, Q2 and K3 (likelihood high) already expect these to conflict. The results doc (rhythm-stability-results.md section 4) says lonley's 32-41% on-place rate is too near the 20% chance rate for a constant to separate, and that penalties, leak, window 0.15 and open score 3 were all tried and rejected. Roughly 9 kicks in 4 s cannot separate 35% from 20% by any beat-level statistic, whether on-place rate (O1) or Rayleigh R (O2/O3). S8 lists these as replay candidates, so it is likely to re-run rejected work. The only candidate that uses different information is bar-to-bar repeat, which the doc names as the lead, and it is listed last.
findings.suggestion: Rewrite AC8 as two tiers: scatter rejection is mandatory (it.fails removed), and the 4 s opening is a target recorded as met or open per D11. Make bar-to-bar repeat the first S8 candidate. Add a replay feasibility check on lonley (kicks available in 4 s versus the statistic's power) before any gate code is written.
findings.resolution: Changed the plan: AC8 and the metric are two-tier, S8 starts with a feasibility check and tries bar-to-bar repeat first.

findings.finding: D5 shows that normalizeOctave folds to 80..160 and 2x is therefore always over 140. D6 halves 'until it fits', so 2x resolves to 1x for every locked tempo up to 140 and to 0.5x above it. dancingCharacterSync.ts:173-177 today halves only when the chosen step is 1. After S3 the slider's top step is identical to the step below it. D7 (planner-assumption) leaves the slider unchanged and says to 'revisit if it reads as broken', so the plan ships a dead control and the AC10 spec for '2x, 1x and calm' pins the equivalence in place. The barsPerLoop < 1 double-time branch (lines 187-195) becomes unreachable while locked. That is dead code under the 95% coverage rule, and S9 will touch the same branch for the crossfade.
findings.suggestion: State in D7 that 2x equals 1x while locked and decide now: remove or relabel the step, or accept it knowingly. In S3, delete the unreachable branch and its specs, or keep it with a stated reason. Say what the calm-rate cap at 2x is, as a number against MAX_DANCE_BPM.
findings.resolution: Asked Trevor: remove the 2x step (D7). S3 deletes the branch; D6 gives the calm cap as about 0.97.

findings.finding: C3/S7 (K4) make a dotted rival held for TEMPO_DOTTED_JUMP_SECONDS at confidence 0.5 or more raise BOUNDARY_SOFT. The only exemption is 'the held tempo corrected at first lock'. The tracker still self-corrects later (a dotted hold needs 32 estimates, tempo.ts:315-331), and S5 may add more late corrections. On syncopation-no-kick (holds 180 for the whole track) or syncopationbass (rival 130.7), a late correction of 180 to 135 would be reported as a song change. That bumps songChangeCount, runs keepOnlyRecent (rhythmAnalyzer.ts:249-258), resets the dance lock, octave and gate (dancingCharacterSync.ts:141-146), and restarts the stability the plan is protecting. eval:rhythm only counts false changes on whole files and cannot see a missed true dotted change, so the 0.00 guard covers only half of AC6. S7 depends only on S4, not on S5.
findings.suggestion: Have the boundary detector follow the tracker's own published-tempo corrections (a rival that the tracker itself adopts re-seeds the reference without a boundary) at any time, not only at first lock. Add a spec 'held tempo corrected 187.5 to 140 at 30 s raises nothing'. Make S7 depend on S5, or at least re-run the six-track false-boundary check after S5.
findings.resolution: Changed the plan with a different fix: re-seeding on every adoption would hide real changes, so D12 and C3 test whether the old pulse's support collapsed. S7 now depends on S5, with a false-boundary recheck and a spec for a correction at 30 s.

findings.finding: C1 and the tie-break component leave TEMPO_TIE_MAX_DEFER_S without a value (O1 had about 3 s, O2 had 8 s). bpm 0 for that long stacks on a 5 s lock and an 11-13 s meter lock, and the beat grid, meter, bass gate and dance lock are all gated on a published tempo. The success metrics and AC8 measure 'after lock', and AC9 measures 'after meter lock', so none of them measures the added delay. O1's risk 'deferral can interact with boundary detection at song start' was dropped in O4 without a replacement, and C1 does not say what boundary.pushTempo receives while deferred. D2 permits slower, but an unbounded budget lets the slice trade away the first-response experience unnoticed.
findings.suggestion: Fix the defer ceiling in C1 (and a ceiling for added time to meter lock), add time-to-first-publish and time-to-meter-lock to the success metrics, and specify the pushTempo input during deferral with a synthetic spec in rhythmAnalyzer.test.ts.
findings.resolution: Changed the plan: D16 sets the ceiling, metrics measure first publish and meter lock, C1 specifies pushTempo during deferral.

findings.finding: S4 (size L, R2) bundles the probe, the tie-break and a conditional escalation to a kick-only vote. The escalation changes the pushFrame signature, adds a data path, and spends bundle headroom of 0.24 kB (K1, K6). AC2, the other success metrics and slices S5-S8 all hang on S4, and nothing says what happens if the probe shows bar repeat does not separate lonley (K1 is medium likelihood and high impact). There is no checkpoint for Trevor between probe and build. S6 (octave re-seed, grid keep) and S8 are needed even when no tie-break works, because corrections still occur, so their dependency on S4 looks like ordering convenience.
findings.suggestion: Split S4 into S4a (probe results written to the results doc, a stop/go with Trevor) and S4b (implementation). Add an explicit branch: if the probe is negative, AC2 is recorded open, S4b is dropped or re-scoped, and S6/S8 proceed on their own. Weaken the S6/S8 dependency to S4a where the code does not need the tie-break.
findings.resolution: Changed the plan: S4 is now the probe with a stop or go, S11 the implementation, D13 the negative branch; S6 and S8 depend only on the probe.

findings.finding: AC2, AC4 (timeScale across plays), AC5 (rebuilds 0), AC8, AC9 and most success metrics can only be checked live on Trevor's machine. The audio is not in the repo, so CI proves only synthetic specs. '4 of 4 fresh plays' is weak evidence for a fault seen in 2 of 3 plays. A tracker that still fails one play in three passes 4 of 4 about 20% of the time. The plays also differ for reasons the doc calls unexplained (frame timing, the 9 s rebuild). There is no stored evidence for a reviewer other than a PR comment.
findings.suggestion: Commit the derived, non-audio onset-sum and kick-flux envelopes (if licensing allows) or at least the telemetry CSVs, so the replay and probe tools give a deterministic regression for the tie-break. Raise the live gate to 8 plays for lonley and syncopationbass, or state that 4 of 4 is a smoke check rather than proof.
findings.resolution: Changed the plan: Trevor agreed to commit derived fixtures (D15, AC13), and the live gate rose to 8 plays.

findings.finding: D8/C5/S9 make the crossfade 'once at meter lock' as a one-shot field on DanceTimingResult. The results doc (section 5) says summer2000 re-locks the meter a beat apart after its break near 23 s, and computeDanceTiming has enter and exit thresholds, so meterLocked can toggle several times per song. Nothing defines a per-song latch, and nothing defines what happens when the one-shot is not consumed (the visualizer is hidden, or the frame is dropped). The previous session chose the capped nudge so the dancer 'never jumps' (doc line 151), and K7 is only 'judged by eye'. Also, the doc says the clip already converges to within 0.01 of the bar after meter lock, so the 0.199-0.533 p95 spread is caused by the catch-up window. AC9's 'after meter lock' window must be pinned to when the metric starts, or the crossfade may not change what debug:repeat reports.
findings.suggestion: Specify the latch (once per songChangeCount, plus an explicit rule for re-lock), who clears the one-shot, and the minimum error threshold in beats. State in AC9 the exact debug:repeat window start. Add a spec for toggling meterLocked.
findings.resolution: Changed the plan: D8 defines the latch and 0.5 beat threshold, C5 the same-frame consumption, AC9 the window start and toggling spec.

findings.finding: The probe in S4 and K5 rest on references that are weak. Q1 (lonley 140 and summer2000 127.5 or 129) is marked non-blocking, but the tie-break and AC2 tune directly against lonley's 140, and the doc says lonley's reference 'has not been confirmed by ear'. If lonley's truth is 187.5 or something else, S4, S6 and AC4 are built on the wrong target. D10's candidates A-F are 'from reading, no run', and D10's claim that the 4L comparison is decisive for a 3-3-3-3-4 pattern is untested. S5's whole premise (a ranked list) is unverified.
findings.suggestion: Make Q1 blocking for S4b (not for S1/S4a): Trevor confirms lonley and summer2000 by ear before any tie-break constant is chosen. Record the probe's tempo columns for the alternative references too, so a wrong reference is visible.
findings.resolution: Asked Trevor: lonley is confirmed at 140 (D14). summer2000 stays open in Q1 and does not drive tuning. D10 stays explicitly untested; S4 records which case applies.

findings.finding: AC1 says ablation 'overrides one rhythmConfig constant deterministically' via an env map (C2, O2), but rhythmConfig.ts exports compile-time constants consumed by ES imports. The plan does not say how an override works without production-code hooks. A hook inside app code would ship in the bundle (0.24 kB headroom) or break the pure-config rule (AGENTS.md rules 2 and 5), while a build-time define or alias in scripts/ is fine. S1 also holds seven tool deliverables as one M slice, although S4 needs only the probe and the telemetry columns, and the telemetry column change touches the debug harness that live checks rely on.
findings.suggestion: State the override mechanism in C2 (esbuild alias or define in scripts/ only; no change in app/) and add a size check showing no app bundle change for S1. Consider splitting the telemetry columns and probe (needed by S4a) from the ablation, gate replay and eval fixes.
findings.resolution: Changed the plan: C2 names the scripts-only plugin with a size check, and S1 was split with S12.

findings.finding: D1 says every slice can be dropped alone, but S10 depends on S5 (a stretch slice), S9 depends on S3 and S6, and the dependency graph does not say what a dropped dependency means. S10 does not list S3, S4 or S6 either. AC12 is therefore unreachable if S5 is dropped, and risk classes are inconsistent: S4 and S8 change the clock at R2, while the gate change that ships a visible behavior to production on every push to main has no rollback trigger beyond 'smoke run fails'.
findings.suggestion: Define 'dropped' in the graph (a dropped dependency counts as satisfied, with the outcome recorded as open), list every slice S10 records, and add one concrete rollback criterion for clock-changing slices (for example, any six-track regression found within a day of deploy).
findings.resolution: Changed the plan: D13 defines a dropped dependency, S10 lists every slice, rollout has a regression trigger.
